title: Detection of Activated Mouse Neurons with Temporal Resolution via Dual c-Fos Staining
protocol: Prepare three exposure cages for each mouse to be exposed.
Label the exposure cages as cage #1, cage #2, and cage #3.
Transfer a third of the soiled bedding from the subject’s home cage to a new clean deodorized cage for Cage #1.
Do not overlay Cage #1 with food compartment/grid or water bottle.
Keep Cage #1 closed with a lid until ready to be used in step 2.
Prepare Cage #2 exactly like Cage #1.
Cage #3 is the animal’s home cage, containing the remaining one-third of soiled bedding.
Remove the food compartment/grid and water bottle from Cage #3 when ready to start the exposure sessions.
Transfer cages #1 to #3 to a dark procedure room without disturbing the animal with loud noises or sudden movements.
Expose the animal to cage #1 in the dark procedure room for 1 hour.
Slowly open the cage lid of cage #1 and insert the first olfactory stimulus source into the cage, on the side opposite to where the animal is located.
Choose an appropriate olfactory stimulus based on experimental interest.
Scent medical gauze or cotton ball with liquid stimuli (urine, saliva, purified odorants, pheromones, recombinant proteins).
Attach scent sources to a binder clip if composed of several pieces to prevent dispersion.
Expose animals to scented substrate for 20 minutes without disturbance.
Use clean cotton ball or medical gauze as control stimulus.
Expose control animals to solid substrate containing neutral odor diluent (PBS or mineral oil) when liquid stimuli are used.
Transfer the animal back to cage #3 (home cage) at the end of the first exposure session.
Let the animal stay undisturbed and unstimulated for 60 min.
Transfer the animal to cage #2.
Immediately insert the second olfactory stimulus source into the cage, on the side opposite to where the animal is located.
Close with a lid and let the exposure proceed for 20 min.
Proceed to the following section immediately after the second exposure window is finished.
Anesthetize the animal intraperitoneally with ketamine and xylazine dissolved in PBS.
Dissect to open the rib cage and expose the cardiac chamber using appropriate tools.
Inject the ventricle with 20 mL of cold PBS.
Inject the ventricle with 40 mL of cold 4% paraformaldehyde fixative prepared in PBS.
Dissect the brain using appropriate tools, exposing the region of interest.
Immerse the dissected brain or brain region in 4% paraformaldehyde fixative.
Ensure the specimen is fully submerged in the fixative solution.
Place the tissue culture plate with a lid at 4°C for fixation (12 to 16 hours).
Remove the fixative solution using a p1000 pipetman or 5 mL serological pipette.
Add enough volume of 20% sucrose in PBS and incubate at 4°C for 2–3 days.
Check that the specimen has sunk to the bottom of the well, indicating successful equilibration.
Remove the sucrose solution.
Add enough volume of cold PBS.
Embed the specimen containing the region of interest in agarose.
Mix 100 mL of 1× PBS with 3.5 g of agarose and 8.0 g of sucrose pellets to prepare the embedding solution.
Dissolve sucrose on a heated plate or in a microwave oven until the solution is homogenous and clear.
Let the solution cool down at 23°C–26°C until it is close to gelation.
Pour the embedding solution onto a plastic histology mold, enough to produce a 0.5–1.0 cm high block.
Blot the desired specimen dry with Kimwipes.
Place the specimen in the embedding mold while the agarose solution is still liquid, using forceps.
Push the specimen down so it touches the bottom of the plastic mold.
Trim the solidified block with a razor blade to have agarose margins approximately 3–5 mm from the specimen edges.
Glue the trimmed block to the vibratome stage with fast-drying Super Glue.
Section through the block on a Leica VT 1000S vibratome under PBS.
Produce 40 μm sections.
Stain the 40 μm sections as free-floating sections in subsequent steps.
Gently pick each section from the vibratome reservoir with a fine paintbrush.
Transfer each section to the wells of a multi-well plate containing PBS.
Collect each section into an individual well for tracking order along the direction of cutting.
Alternatively, collect sets of sections into each well.
Store sections in PBS at 4°C for up to 2 days.
Fill the required number of wells in an RNase-free 12-well plate with RNase-free PBS.
Choose suitable sections and transfer them to the plate with a paintbrush.
Place a maximum of three sections per well.
Remove PBS and wash sections twice with 1× PBS, for 5 min each, under gentle agitation on a plate rocker.
Remove PBS and add 4% paraformaldehyde prepared in 1× PBS.
Treat sections under agitation for 20 minutes.
Wash sections twice in 1× PBS under agitation.
Permeabilize sections with 0.2 M HCl prepared in RNase-free ultrapure water.
Incubate the permeabilized sections at 23°C–26°C under agitation for 10 minutes.
Wash sections twice in 1× PBS under agitation.
Inactivate endogenous peroxidases by incubating sections in 0.1% H2O2 prepared in RNase-free 1× PBS.
Incubate the sections at 23°C–26°C under agitation, in the dark for 30 minutes.
Calculate the volume needed for pre-hyb phase by multiplying 300 μL by the number of wells to be stained, and dispense in a conical tube.
Heat the pre-hyb solution at 58°C until ready to use.
Aliquot hybridization solution as 300 μl fractions in 1.5 ml microfuge tubes.
Heat each fraction to 85°C for 15 min prior to use.
Wash sections twice in 1× PBS under agitation, for 5 min each.
Prepare acetylation solution by mixing 20 ml of 0.1 M triethanolamine-HCl pH 8.0 with 50 μl of acetic anhydride.
Add 1 ml of acetylation solution per well and pipette 2 μL of concentrated acetic anhydride per well.
Gently mix on a plate rocker for 10 min.
Wash sections twice in 1× PBS under agitation, for 5 min each.
Transfer the plate to a humidified chamber at 58°C.
Equilibrate sections to the pre-hyb temperature by incubating in 1× PBS at 58°C for 5 min.
Pre-hybridize sections with at least 300 μL of pre-warmed pre-hyb solution at 58°C for 1 hour in a humidified chamber.
Place the plate on railings and close the plate lid before sealing the chamber.
Remove the plate from the humidified chamber when changing solutions at 58°C, place it on a heated block, and return to the sealed chamber immediately after change.
Ten minutes prior to end of pre-hybridization step, mix pre-warmed hybridization solution with two 1 kb digoxigenin-labeled cRNA riboprobes for detection of c-Fos mRNA.
Quickly mix by inversion and place tube containing probes and hyb solution at 85°C for denaturation for 5-10 minutes.
Remove pre-hyb solution from each well and add probe-containing working hybridization solution (300 μL per well).
Ensure sections lay flat at the bottom of each well during hybridization; unfold with a paintbrush if necessary.
Return the plate to the humidified chamber.
Close the plate lid.
Seal the chamber.
Place it back at 58°C.
Perform hybridization for 16 hours.
Pre-warm 2× SSC, 0.2× SSC, and 0.1× SSC to 55°C.
Lower the temperature of the humidified chamber to 55°C by transferring it to another bath or oven for 15 minutes.
Remove hybridization solution from each well at a time.
Add 500 μL of pre-warmed 2× SSC wash solution.
Incubate for 30 minutes with occasional manual agitation.
Perform sequential washes in 0.2× SSC and 0.1× SSC at 55°C, for 20 minutes each.
Remove the humidified chamber from the bath or oven.
Replace solution in each well with 0.1× SSC at 23°C–26°C.
Incubate for 3–5 minutes to equilibrate sections to 23°C–26°C.
Permeabilize in PTw solution at 23°C–26°C for 10 minutes.
Perform washes and incubations under gentle agitation.
Equilibrate sections in TN buffer by performing two washes at 23°C–26°C for 5 minutes each.
Block sections in TNB buffer at 23°C–26°C for 3 hours.
Incubate sections in TNB buffer containing horseradish-peroxidase-conjugated anti-digoxigenin antibody (1:400; Merck/Roche) at 4°C for 2 days in a sealed humidified chamber.
Prepare a fresh working solution of antibody solution for immunodetection.
Ensure the humidified chamber contains Kimwipes wetted with PBS or water.
Wash each well six times in TNT buffer for 5 minutes each under gentle agitation at 23°C-26°C.
Mix amplification diluent, H2O2 (final concentration 0.0015%), and tyramide-biotin (1:50) to prepare the solution fresh immediately before use.
Incubate sections in tyramide-biotin solution for 15 minutes at 23°C-26°C.
Overlay a round piece of Parafilm onto the well if using less than 150 μL of solution.
Wash each well six times in TNT buffer for 5 minutes each under gentle agitation at 23°C-26°C.
Incubate sections in TNB buffer containing peroxidase-conjugated streptavidin at 1:100 dilution for 1 hour.
Wash sections 6 times in TNT buffer for 5 minutes each under gentle agitation.
Prepare tyramide-Alexa 555 fluorescent development reagent by mixing amplification diluent with H2O2 and tyramide-Alexa 555 at the specified concentrations.
Incubate sections in tyramide-Alexa 555 solution for 15 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash sections 6 times in TNT buffer for 5 minutes each under gentle agitation.
Permeabilize sections in 0.3% Triton X-100/1× PBS for 10 min.
Perform a first blocking step in 1% blocking reagent (Thermo) for 1 h at 23°C–26°C under gentle agitation.
Perform a second blocking step in 0.3% Triton X-100/1% BSA/1× PBS for 30 min at 23°C–26°C under gentle agitation.
Incubate sections in anti-c-Fos antibody solution [0.3% Triton X-100/1% BSA/1× PBS containing anti-c-Fos antibody (1:1500; Ab2; Millipore)] for 2 days at 4°C, under gentle agitation.
Wash sections three times in 0.1% Triton X-100/1× PBS, for 15 min each.

Incubate in anti-rabbit secondary antibody solution [0.3% Triton X-100/1% BSA/1× PBS containing Alexa 488-conjugated anti-rabbit secondary antibody (1:500; Thermo)] for 3 h at 23°C–26°C, under gentle agitation.
Incubate sections in 3% H2O2/1× PBS for 1 h to inactivate peroxidases from previous steps.
Incubate sections in 0.1 M HCl/0.9% NaCl for 15 min.
Wash sections 6 times in TNT buffer, for 5 min each.
Permeabilize sections in 0.3% Triton X-100/1× PBS for 10 min.
Perform a first blocking step in 1% blocking reagent (Thermo) for 1 h at 23°C–26°C under gentle agitation.
Perform a second blocking step in 0.3% Triton X-100/1% BSA/1× PBS for 30 min at 23°C–26°C under gentle agitation.
Incubate in anti-c-Fos antibody solution for 2 days at 4°C under gentle agitation.
Wash sections three times in 0.1% Triton X-100/1× PBS, for 15 minutes each.
Wash sections for an additional 15 minutes with 1× PBS to remove Triton X-100.
Incubate with peroxidase-conjugated anti-rabbit secondary antibody in 1% blocking reagent for 1 hour at 23°C–26°C.
Wash three times with 1× PBS, for 15 minutes each.
Prepare enough volume of tyramide-Alexa 488 fluorescent development reagent by mixing amplification diluent with H2O2 and tyramide-Alexa 488.
Incubate sections in tyramide-Alexa 488 solution for 5–10 minutes at 23°C–26°C.
Wash three times with 1× PBS, for 15 minutes each.
Counterstain with TO-PRO-3 iodide solution in 1× PBS for 15 minutes.
Optional: If the confocal microscope used contains a UV laser, sections may be counterstained with DAPI or Hoechst 33342.
Wash twice in 1× PBS, for 5 minutes each.
Pipette 1 mL of 1× PBS onto a glass microscope slide.
Use a fine paintbrush to transfer each stained section to the pool formed by PBS.
Unfold the sections and apply pressure to make them sink to the bottom of the pool and adhere to the glass slide.
Carefully remove PBS from the microscope slide using a p1000 pipetman, ensuring sections are not disturbed or made to overlap with each other.
Remove excess liquid by tilting the slide and gently touching a piece of Kimwipes.
Pipette 100–150 μL of ProLong Gold antifade mounting reagent.
Carefully and slowly overlay with a 24 x 60 mm glass coverslip, without introducing air bubbles.
Maintain the slides at 23°C–26°C or at 4°C for at least 12 hours in a dry container protected from light.
Mount stained sections onto a glass microscope slide.
Image the sections using a confocal microscope or equivalent imaging technique.
Collect images as a z-series with either a 40× or a 63× planar objective, under oil.
Ensure each optical section is less than 0.5 μm thick.
Produce maximum intensity projection images across the z-series to visualize c-Fos mRNA staining and co-localization with c-Fos protein immunostaining.
